name: Tourist eVisa

requirements.blocker_text: Only nationals of the roughly 66 countries on the eVisa eligibility list can apply online; other nationalities must use a Saudi embassy/consulate visa or a licensed travel agent instead.
requirements.fix_path: Apply through a Saudi embassy or consulate if not on the eVisa-eligible list.

requirements.blocker_text: The eVisa covers tourism, Umrah (excluding Hajj, which has a separate seasonal visa), family and friend visits, and attending events; it does not authorise any form of paid work.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the relevant work or business route instead if the purpose is employment.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a passport valid for at least 6 months and mandatory travel medical insurance, bundled into the eVisa fee.
requirements.fix_path: Renew the passport if fewer than 6 months of validity remain.

evidence_required.document: Online application via visa.visitsaudi.com, processed in 24-72 hours

outcome.duration_length: 1 year multiple-entry, up to 90 days per visit
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: max 90 days per visit within the 1-year multiple-entry validity

sources.title: visa.visitsaudi.com -- official Saudi Arabia eVisa portal (Ministry of Tourism / General Directorate of Passports)
Saudia (national carrier, government-owned) -- Tourist Visa requirements, corroborating the passport-validity and age conditions

notes: Saudi Arabia's eVisa, launched September 2019, represents one of the fastest visa-regime liberalisations in this dataset -- from essentially closed to tourism to a 66-country eVisa list within a few years, explicitly framed against a Vision 2030 target of 150 million annual visits by 2030. Distinguished from the separate seasonal Hajj visa (not modeled as its own route file here, since it is a religious-pilgrimage-specific, quota-managed, government-coordinated process rather than an ordinary applicant-facing immigration route, and sits closer to a logistics/quota allocation system than a comparable route) and from the Business Visit Visa (valid up to 90 days, permits meetings and negotiations but explicitly prohibits any ongoing work relationship -- flagged as a candidate for a future separate route file rather than folded in here, since its requirement grammar differs meaningfully from tourism).
